artworks.title: A Pair of Marble Benches
artworks.dimensions: H 40.5 inches · W 77 inches · D 28 inches
artworks.description: A pair of marble benches with lions' bodies for arms and back molding of edge and dart design. The seat supports of winged lions are after a Greek original in the Vatican, Rome.They are original to "Rosecliff" and originally aligned on a north-south axis flanking a path to fountain.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mr. J. Edgar Monroe, 1971.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Rose garden south of the house, with gravel paths (outline from OpenStreetMap)
artworks.placeNote: Made for Rosecliff’s garden, where they flanked a path to a fountain (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection) (our guess: the Society doesn’t say which room it is in today).

artworks.title: Italy
artworks.description: Titled "Italy" or "Reminiscence of the Bay of Salerno," an oil on canvas coastal scene by John Frederick Kensett (American, 1816-1872). Taking place at either sunrise or sunset, the scene depicts an avenue of trees with figures in the left middle ground, a ravine runs to the beach and a prominent ruined fortress stands along the cliffs leading to the coast, the sea with boats on it is on the right side of the canvas, and the rising/setting sun is reflected on the water.The remains of a label on the back of the frame reads "Museum of Art" and is annotated 248, from the exhibition of the painting titled "Italy" and numbered 248 in the Loan Collection of Paintings in the West and East Galleries, Oct. 1880 to March 1880, Metropolitan Museum of Art. The catalogue notes the painting as property of Robert Hoe, a printing press tycoon. Also shown at the Spring exhibition of the National Academy of Design in 1867 (no. 499) when it had already been purchased by Hoe. Formerly identified at the time of acquisition as View of the Capri Coast.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mr. J. Edgar Monroe.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.placeNote: In the Dining Room (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: Bronze Renaissance Style Figurehead of a Winged Amor with Dolphin
artworks.dimensions: H 29 inches · W 15 inches · D 15 inches
artworks.description: A patinated bronze renaissance style figurehead of a winged amor with dolphin by Janet Scudder (American, 1869-1940). The figure of young standing cherub or "Amor" is astride a dolphin that was adapted as a fountainhead.The subject of children with animals was inspired by Italian Renaissance sculpture.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mr. J. Edgar Monroe, 1971.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Forecourt garden on the Bellevue Avenue side, with its fountain (the plan’s “Garden”)
artworks.placeNote: A fountain figure Theresa Oelrichs owned (our guess: the Society doesn’t say which room it is in today).
